column1: # FIRST FP COVERAGE OF SEQUENTIAL CVA6 DESIGNS.
# Until this run every design in the FP evidence had ZERO flops (section 46).
# `proto_probe --support` accepts 22 of the 29 frozen-30 certificates present in
# cva6_30_auth; 8 of those 22 already had FP evidence, and ALL 14 of the rest are
# sequential.  This is the covered backend -- total_probe, `Projection.mixDriver`
# + `hwAPVarT`, the pair for which IHwAdequate_varT, specializeDesign_varT_correct
# and simSound_varT are proved -- run on all 14 at fuel 200000/2000 under an 8 GiB
# named scope with a 1800 s cap, through pass/lean/scripts/fp_replay.py, whose
# admission boundary is the one its 40 controls exercise.
# RESULT: 8 of 14 ADMITTED, all 8 sequential (11 to 71 flops).  The other 6 were
# stopped by the WALL CLOCK and are recorded as RESOURCE STOP, undecided -- never
# as failures.  None was an OOM: cgroup memory.events reports oom_kill 0 on all
# 14, and the worst peak was csr_regfile at 1.29 GB against the 8 GiB cap.
# All 14 report support_all true, and all 6 stopped runs had already finished
# specializing, so the cap fell during the stimulus phase.
# WHAT SEPARATES THEM IS RESIDUAL SIZE, NOT FLOP COUNT OR SOURCE COUNT.
# Every admitted design has a residual of at most 1,600,933 terms; every stopped
# one has at least 2,473,580.  Flop count does not separate them (id_stage, 30
# flops and 10,503 sources, is admitted at 1377 s; issue_read_operands, 89 flops
# and 6,172 sources, is not), and neither does source count.
# SCOPE.  These are pre-D2 DCERT1 certificates, so every one carries the raw-port
# reset-polarity opposition of section 46: the read side and the commit side name
# the same port with opposite polarity.  The AGREEMENT results are unaffected --
# residual and interpretDesign consume the same certificate, so both sides apply
# the same inconsistent polarity -- but `states-reached` here is NOT behavioural
# coverage, because one reset path is asserted throughout.
# NO MANIFEST ROWS WERE ADDED for these runs.  record_experiment.py reads the
# exit from a /usr/bin/time trailer INSIDE the log, which fp_replay does not
# write (it keeps the status in a separate attempt-scoped .exit file).  Recording
# them would produce rows marked `exit None, MISSING ... status is UNKNOWN`,
# which is WEAKER evidence than this join, not stronger.  The join below carries
# the derived outer and worker status, the attempt binding and the guard
# observations.
# runner binary
# binary_sha256
# mode
# fuel
# build
# Every credited field is DERIVED from a file of THIS attempt; the
# attempt id scopes them, so an earlier run's status cannot be read
# as this one's. Identity is bound by FULL sha256. wall_s is the RUN's
# duration from .wall, never the parser's elapsed time. Guard metadata
# is REQUESTED and OBSERVED separately; absent observations stay absent.
